Truck Heists

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
a new breed of thieves, not only stealing the goods, but your company's identity in the process.

Summary:
These criminals steal transporter's details and then poach their work. But it doesn't end there... they steal the loads often worth hundreds of thousands of rands - disappearing without a trace.

In the last two years, investigators have linked over 100 cases to the same illusive criminals.


Further information:
Two of the key players were caught 2 weeks ago - the man believed to be the kingpin had invoice books and delivery notes on him along with the cellphones used for setting up the theft. He is a civil engineer in Fourways.

Since his arrest, the remaining members of the gang have gone into over drive mode, stealing 7 loads in just a week and a half.

Following another tip off, two more members of the gang were arrested this last weekend. BUT were suspiciously released by a cop, who was off duty and has a previous case of corruption against him.

We have information of where these loads are going to and who's raking in the cash.

The last 7 loads that were stolen were all maize and grains taken to AFGRI - the loads were accepted and AFGRI paid out to three "farmers". We follow the trail and expose this criminal ring.


WHAT WE HAVE:
- Footage of the second batch of criminals delivering the loads to AFGRI
- voice recording of setting up the second sting.
- Surveillance photos from the first sting and arrests.
- Surveillance photos from the second sting.

Press Release:


Trucking thieves
The trucking trade brings in big money and criminals know this all too well. Carte Blanche follows the trail of a new breed of thieves, who, dissatisfied with only taking a truck’s cargo, also steal a company’s identity and even use it to rob the victim’s clients.


Script:


TRANSPORT CONS STRUCTURE


VO: In 2014 the road freight industry moved R456 billion worth of goods on our roads – it’s big business for legitimate companies and cunning criminals.

LINK: Pellets, groceries, cooking oil, fertiliser, coffins, yes coffins, because if it can be moved these guys will steal it.

VO: Gangs posing as credible transporters are raking in millions in stolen goods - crippling the industry in the process.

Having investigated over fifty of these cases, totaling R15 million in the last two years alone – Insurance Loss Adjuster, Glynn Millard says it’s a national problem.

BONGANI: How have they been getting away with it for so long?
GLYNN: // they have chopped and changed names all the time, they will use one company today, and tomorrow they are using a different company. They use different cellphone numbers, // there’s no physical address to go to.
BONGANI: SO they hit you and they disappear.
GLYNN: They just disappear, the cellphones are switched off and they are gone.

VO: Determined to catch the thieves, Glynn teamed up with PI Wouter van der Merwe. Finally in January this year, they had a breakthrough.

They were able to intercept a steel coil like this one, valued at around R160 000, set to be collected by a suspected fake transporter in Durban.

They tracked the load all the way to Gauteng.

WOUTER: // we made contact with suspects contact number and he gave us plausible answers and what the delays were for the delivery – how ever the suspect wasn’t aware that we were monitoring him and had eyes on the loads at the time.

VO: //The truck ended up at a legitimate crane company in Benoni – not the intended destination on the delivery note. Wouter, along with a team from Organised Crime KZN, staked out the premises, keeping a watchful eye on the load.

WOUTER: things started getting interesting when the second target vehicle arrived and they started loading the coil – then we knew we were in business because the coil was going to a different location.

VO: The coil was moved to a steel manufacturer in Wadeville.

LINK: There could any number of reasons why a transporter could change vehicle on route to a delivery destination – so it was here when the steel was brought here to be offloaded and cut that the actual crime had been committed, because this is not the address on the delivery note.

VO: Three men were arrested and the steel coil was recovered.

WOUTER: The main suspect was found to be in possession of documents and the actual cellphone that was linked to arranging to all the thefts and losses pertaining to these cases.

VO: The main suspect is Aleck Ndlovu - previously arrested in 2009 for theft of goods in transit and the docket disappeared.

In this current case, he was granted bail of R50 000. We called him for an interview.

UPSOUND CALL:
ALECK: Don’t phone me, you phone my lawyer if you want to discuss anything.

VO: His lawyer said they will comment in court.

This new MO takes identity theft to a whole new level.

LINK: They steal your reputation, your company profile and your clients and there’s almost no defence against it and just like that you’ve been turned into a company of thieves.

VO: Transporter Renier Erasmus, got the shock of his life in March 2013 when his company was accused of stealing cargo loads.

RENIER: a lady called us and say there is a guy that go around with my company details // he claim he // is the manager of RS Regal and he go around and take loads from my customers//.

VO: In just two months, the man picked up at least 10 loads across the country fraudulently using Renier’s company name //.

RENIER: The real loss to my business is huge, you can’t recover that ever – because I mean my business name is jeopardise, people lost trust in my business

VO: While the thieves got away with about R4 million of goods, they also took Renier’s company’s 16 year reputation with them. He lost out on all his cross border transportation contracts.

LINK: Your reputation is everything, especially to the enterprising criminal, because in the cargo freight sector, not everyone will do business with a new company, // you need the credibility of an established business.

VO: In Renier’s case the criminals had all of his company details – from registration numbers to tax numbers, vehicle registrations and driver details – absolutely everything.

BONGANI: Are you angry about this?
RENIER: Of course I am! And the sad thing don’t trust people // because here you can see it was used against me.

VO: Renier is just one of hundreds of companies affected.

GLYNN: // we can’t discount the possibility that they are splinter syndicates working

VO: While Aleck Ndlovu was behind bars awaiting his bail hearing in the steel coil case, there was a sudden spike in grain thefts.

One of the companies hit belongs to Berno Ploeg’s.

BERNO: We’ve basically lost two loads of wheat that we were transporting for a company that we do business for and these loads wasn’t delivered.

VO: Glynn believes the cases could be linked.

GLYNN: They are using the same names to get the loads, they are using transport companies on a regular basis, they are using the information that they have.

VO: Glynn and Wouter teamed up again by setting up a sting offering a controlled load to the suspected grain thieves.

PRODUCT: Maize
LOADING POINT: Schuttesdraai, Free State.
DESTINATION: Howick, KZN

The crooks took the bait and off they went.

WOUTER: we had formulated a surveillance team, // and we followed the two trucks you see behind me from the loading point in Schutte’s draai,

UPSOUND: TRANSPORT BROKER: What time will you be in Howick
CROOK: I think around 7.

VO: But the trucks diverted from their intended route and headed straight for the Afgri Silos in Bronkhorstspruit.

When they stopped to offload – Wouter and the team arrested two drivers – and opened a case of theft against them.

LINK: These are the trucks that delivered the grain, // but if you ask around the silos, the vehicles and the driver are well known to everyone – because they’ve been here before.

WOUTER: they are quick in, quick out fly by nights.

VO: It was a huge win for Wouter and the team – the suspects agreed to cooperate.

WOUTER: We actually spoke to members on call at Bronkhorstspruit and we made explicit entries that the members from Organised Crime KZN will come and do the interview and that no one was supposed to conduct any form of investigation on that docket.

VO: But it didn’t end like that…

LINK: The suspects were released from the Bronkhorstpruit Police station on R500 police bail – something highly regular when one considers the magnitude of the changes.

VO: Gauteng Head of Communication, Col. Noxolo Kweza was too busy for an on-camera interview and sent a written response.

She stated that: Police procedure allows police officials to grant bail to suspects.

This is correct - Bail at a police station is permitted in terms of the Criminal Procedure Act – provided that the value of the stolen goods does not exceed R2500. In this case the value of the stolen maize was R170 000.00.

GLYNN: //A lot of hard work went into get that arrest and to see them walk out and carry on probably doing what they were doing before – it’s disappointing. INT 4 M6

VO: Col. Kweza confirmed that an internal disciplinary investigation has been launched following our queries.

But the real question is who paid the thieves for the loads of maize?

LINK: In agricultural terms, a silo is a type of grain bank, credited every time you make a deposit and you pay for storage, but it’s not really their obligation to check where the grain comes from or where it goes once it leaves.

VO: According to the drivers the delivery was for a Mr. PJ Jordaan – a supplier registered with Afgri.

We tracked him down to his petrol station in Springs.

BONGANI: We’ve got allegations, essentially what we’re being told is that you’re buying stolen goods.
PJ: Oh am I?

VO: He refused to come out of his office and hid behind the door.

BONGANI: There’s stuff, as you know, is confiscated by the police that you bought.
PJ: Yes, that I bought,
BONGANI: which you bought…
PJ: no I haven’t bought it yet

VO: The company listed as supplying him the maize is K Farms. A company PJ believes is legitimate.

BONGANI: you are a part of this thing, you’ve just told me now that you’ve buying for them for a long time…
PJ: yes I have, I don’t deny it. there’s a legal thing coming about this any way – everything I say will be public record, am I right? And it can put me in a bad light.
Bongani: are there charges against you
PJ: not yet, no

VO: He declined to comment any further.

It would seem that the supposed maize supplier, K Farms, has some explaining to do. The company’s only registered director is a Mr. Menzi Zikalala.

We traced the company to this address, also in Springs.

BONGANI: Is it offices?
ELIAS: - no
BONGANI: Is it a private home?
Elias - No, home, it’s empty
Bongani: have you heard of K Farms?
Elias - I don’t know K Farms
Bongani – you don’t know Menzi?
Elias – No,
BONGANI:you don’t know Menzi Zikalale?
ELIAS: Ah-eh.

VO: Clearly this is not where K Farms operates from – we called Mr. Zikalala. He denied knowing anything about the company.

Menzi: I don’t know that, because I don’t even have a bank account – I am unemployed.

VO: Menzi also said that he had lost his ID document last year and that he has never met a PJ Jordaan.

LINK: No way of determining if Menzi is telling the truth but given the way these syndicates operates, it seems like it’s a multi layered operation that targets all sorts of unsuspecting people.

GLYNN: it’s not just a little theft here and there – each incident is probably at least R300 000 or more – insurance companies are not going to be able to sustain these kind of losses – and they’re increasing continually// INT 4 M5










PROMOS

PROMO 1 – 15 seconds
VO: Cunning criminals target transport businesses – stealing their company profile and then robbing their clients.

RENIER: The real loss to my business is huge, you can’t recover that ever – // people lost trust in my business

PROMO 2 – 15 seconds
VO: Trucking is big business especially for cunning criminals.

GLYNN: we’ve dealt with coffins, sugar, coal, timber, anything – you name it, they’ll take it.

VO: We investigates a new breed of transport thieves that hijack entire company identities.

PROMO 3 – 10 seconds
VO: Gangs posing as credible truck companies are raking in millions in stolen goods - crippling transporters in the process.

WOUTER: they are quick in, quick out fly by night operators.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): a new breed of thieves, not only stealing the goods, but your company's identity in the process.
metadata.Summary: These criminals steal transporter's details and then poach their work. But it doesn't end there... they steal the loads often worth hundreds of thousands of rands - disappearing without a trace. In the last two years, investigators have linked over 100 cases to the same illusive criminals.
metadata.Further information: Two of the key players were caught 2 weeks ago - the man believed to be the kingpin had invoice books and delivery notes on him along with the cellphones used for setting up the theft. He is a civil engineer in Fourways. Since his arrest, the remaining members of the gang have gone into over drive mode, stealing 7 loads in just a week and a half. Following another tip off, two more members of the gang were arrested this last weekend. BUT were suspiciously released by a cop, who was off duty and has a previous case of corruption against him. We have information of where these loads are going to and who's raking in the cash. The last 7 loads that were stolen were all maize and grains taken to AFGRI - the loads were accepted and AFGRI paid out to three "farmers". We follow the trail and expose this criminal ring. WHAT WE HAVE: - Footage of the second batch of criminals delivering the loads to AFGRI - voice recording of setting up the second sting. - Surveillance photos from the first sting and arrests. - Surveillance photos from the second sting.
